lane: A-062 PE billing portal, the live-money blocker
status: complete — every acceptance item met and verified by violation in both directions
missionPremise: apps/property-explorer/public/terms.html states verbatim 'You can cancel a paid plan through the Stripe billing flow in the product.' Zero billing-portal references existed anywhere in apps/property-explorer, and SettingsModal.tsx said 'Not built' to the user's face on payment method, invoices and cancellation. The product was honest and the legal page was not, which is the inversion of the usual failure and the half carrying legal weight, because the terms are the document a customer is held to and holds us to. Operator Nick ruled this a BLOCKING Phase 0 item on the Stripe live switch on 2026-08-31, and ruled that the promise is KEPT and the capability BUILT rather than the sentence amended. Source: the card, _inbox/2026-08-31_p97_stripe_live_activation_checklist.md Phase 0 item 3, and _smartsite_gtm/06_consolidated_roadmap.md Wave 1.1.
completionPredicate: A signed-in paying customer can open the Stripe billing portal from Settings, on their own customer id, and cancel. A signed-in customer who has never paid gets an honest refusal rather than a portal, an error, or somebody else's account. The sentence in terms.html is true, and a check fails if the two halves drift apart again. A stranger evaluates this by running the two named test commands and by reading the seven acceptance items against the evidence table below; nothing in it requires taking this lane's word for anything.
scopeBasis: The card's seven acceptance items, and no more. The route, its client, the allowlist line, the Settings row, and the anti-drift check are in. Explicitly excluded and left untouched, each because the card says so: terms.html is not amended (the ruling is keep the promise); api/pe-billing.ts is not retired (Wave 1.2, and the P-103 seam lane holds those files); the install-scoped POST /api/brokerage/v1/billing/portal route and the extension portal path are not touched; no Stripe live switch and no live Stripe object; no dunning, invoice history or payment-method UI beyond linking to Stripe's own portal. One thing NOT in the card was done and is declared as a finding rather than buried: a latent fail-closed defect in the code being reused (F1 below).

acceptanceItems.title: No customer id is a declared refusal, never a fabricated one
acceptanceItems.built: createPeBillingPortalSession returns a discriminated-union arm { kind: 'no-billing-account' }; the route maps it to 409 { error: 'no_billing_account', hasBillingAccount: false, message }. acceptanceItems.proof: src/lib/proxy-allowlist.test.ts imports BILLING_PORTAL_PATH from ./portalClient — the constant the client builds its request from, not a retyped string — and asserts isDeepPathAllowed('POST', BILLING_PORTAL_PATH) is true. acceptanceItems.title: The return URL points at Smart Site

acceptanceItems.title: Settings > Plan replaces 'Not built' with a working control, and only where it is working
acceptanceItems.built: The three rows Payment method / Invoices / Cancel subscription collapse into ONE row, 'Payment, invoices and cancellation', because they are three doors into the same Stripe Customer Portal rather than three features we own. The control renders ONLY on billingManagementState === 'manage'. 'none' renders 'No billing history' with a sentence; 'unread' renders 'Not read'. Renewal date is UNCHANGED and still says Not read, because that value is genuinely not on the entitlement wire.
acceptanceItems.proof: billingManagementState is a pure exported function tested across all three arms and every non-ready outcome (null, sign-in, blocked, not-built, error, and an authenticated:false 200). It is NOT derived from tier: a paid account whose customer id never landed reads 'none' honestly, and a FREE account that subscribed once and cancelled reads 'manage', which is exactly the person most likely to want the portal.
acceptanceItems.whyNotARenderTest: renderToStaticMarkup runs no effects, so the account read never resolves and the 'manage' arm is unreachable in a render test. The render test proves the complementary half — first paint shows Not read and NOT the button — and the pure function proves the rest.
acceptanceItems.scopeDiscipline: settings-plan-rows.test.tsx's old guard counted exactly three 'Not built' strings to catch a fourth row being lit up by accident. It now asserts ZERO 'Not built' anywhere on the tab, which is a strictly stronger guard: a future card cannot add one back silently.

LESSON: String(x) is never a presence check. `const v = String(obj.field); if (!v) throw` cannot fire, because String(undefined) is the truthy string "undefined". This shipped in the install-scoped Stripe portal and would have redirected a customer to a page named "undefined". Read the field and test its type.

A refusal and a silent ignore have the same security outcome and opposite evidential value. Ignoring a caller-supplied customer id protects the account and leaves the attempt indistinguishable from an ordinary request in every log. Refuse, and name the source in the error, so the attempt is counted.

When two checks guard the same thing, assert the SPECIFIC failure, not merely that it failed. Disabling this lane's named customer-id check still produced a 4xx via the strict schema; only an assertion on the error string caught the loss.

A render test cannot reach state that arrives via an effect. renderToStaticMarkup runs no effects, so any assertion about a resolved async read has to live on a pure exported function instead. Settings already had this shape (accessLabel, ladderEntitlementFromAccount) and the new rule follows it.

An anti-drift check between a promise and a capability needs BOTH directions injected. Removing the capability must fail it, and so must removing the promise — otherwise deleting the sentence is a quiet way to make the whole check vacuous.
